why: Deconstructs pervasive e-commerce myths, explaining why platform-reported ROAS and Klaviyo's attributed revenue models are fundamentally flawed as primary performance metrics, and advocating for base-reality analytics like incrementality testing to properly measure retention and paid media impact.
topics: [attribution and modeling, business and marketing analytics]

attribution and modeling / Debunking the use of Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) and Klaviyo's default attributed revenue as primary KPIs for e-commerce growth. Explaining that ROAS is a flawed metric because it relies on last-click attribution (failing to capture top-of-funnel awareness), is easily skewed by existing customers, and drives misallocation of budget toward bottom-of-funnel retargeting rather than incremental acquisition. Clarifying that Klaviyo's default attribution (e.g., 5-day open, 5-day click) acts essentially as a view-through metric, inflating top-line email revenue by taking credit for high-intent returning customers who would have purchased regardless of the email interaction.

business and marketing analytics / Addressing the limitations of using paid media as a retention channel, noting that retargeting existing customers on Meta often yields an inflated ROAS but drives negligible incremental revenue, as revealed by conversion lift experiments (geo-holdouts). Advocating for "base reality" measurement frameworks that evaluate true incrementality, net profit, and Customer Lifetime Value (CLTV) across all contexts, rather than relying on nuanced, context-dependent platform metrics that do not directly influence the bottom line. Emphasizing that low customer retention is fundamentally a structural business or product quality issue, not a problem that can be fixed simply by optimizing email flows.

The primary flaw of using ROAS as a core KPI: it relies on last-click attribution, over-credits bottom-of-funnel retargeting, and masks true incremental acquisition. The danger of targeting existing customers with paid media: it often generates high ROAS but very low incremental revenue. The limitation of Klaviyo's default attribution settings (e.g., 5-day open/click): it functions largely as a view-through metric, inflating attributed revenue by taking credit for purchases from returning customers who were already going to buy.
General commentary on the shift from growth-at-all-costs mentalities to profit-focused models in the post-COVID era. Critiques of e-commerce coaching groups or "gurus."
